knowledge:
- key_parameters: data.type=specifies the type of copy number data (e.g., "logratio") ;; sampleid=identifier for the sample ;; verbose=controls progress output during segmentation ;; undo.splits=method to remove unnecessary splits (e.g., "sdundo") ;; undo.SD=number of standard deviations for the sdundo method ;; plot.type=type of plot ("w" for whole genome, "s" for single-study by chromosome, "p" for plateaus ordered by segment means, "c" for chromosome across studies) ;; p.method=method to calculate p-values ("perm" for full permutation, default is hybrid) ;; nperm=number of permutations for the hybrid method ;; alpha=significance level for accepting change-points
- alternatives: p.method='perm'=runs the full permutation analysis instead of the default hybrid approach (recommended only if the hybrid approach is not desired, though the hybrid approach is much faster)
- when_to_use: Appropriate for analyzing array DNA copy number data (such as array CGH) to identify genomic regions of gained and lost copy number by finding change-points.
- pitfalls: Single point outliers can bias segmentation and should be smoothed using smooth.CNA before running segment ;; Local trends can cause false change-points, requiring an undo method like sdundo to remove unnecessary splits ;; Overlapping windows are no longer recommended for larger datasets ;; Lowering alpha requires more permutations (nperm), and the stopping boundary must be computed (automatically or via getbdry) if non-default nperm and alpha are used

workflows.name: dna_copy_number_segmentation
workflows.intent: Segment DNA copy number data to identify genomic regions with abnormal copy number using circular binary segmentation (CBS).
input: copy_number_data.txt (tab-delimited file containing sample log-ratios, chromosome numbers, and physical positions)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the DNAcopy package and import data into a CNA object using CNA() ;; 2. Smooth single-point outliers using smooth.CNA() ;; 3. Segment the smoothed data using segment() ;; 4. Visualize the segmented data using plot() with different plot.type options ;; 5. Refine segmentation by undoing splits with segment() using undo.splits="sdundo" and plot the results
workflows.code:
library(DNAcopy)
data(coriell)
CNA.object <- CNA(cbind(coriell$Coriell.05296),
                  coriell$Chromosome,coriell$Position,
                  data.type="logratio",sampleid="c05296")
smoothed.CNA.object <- smooth.CNA(CNA.object)
segment.smoothed.CNA.object <- segment(smoothed.CNA.object, verbose=1)
plot(segment.smoothed.CNA.object, plot.type="w")
plot(segment.smoothed.CNA.object, plot.type="s") 
plot(segment.smoothed.CNA.object, plot.type="p")
sdundo.CNA.object <- segment(smoothed.CNA.object, 
                             undo.splits="sdundo", 
                             undo.SD=3,verbose=1)
plot(sdundo.CNA.object,plot.type="s")
